introduction.value: A reviewer ran Meta's Muse Wonder through inbox triage, email batching, and long-term research, naming it her favorite across four agentic tasks, with weaker creative output.

method.value: Claire Vo signed up for Meta's model API access and installed the Muse Code command-line tool. source_text.body:
Triage inbox and batch email with an agent model
A reviewer ran Meta's Muse Wonder through inbox triage, email batching, and long-term research, naming it her favorite across four agentic tasks, with weaker creative output.
Done with
MM
Meta Muse
What they did
Claire Vo signed up for Meta's model API access and installed the Muse Code command-line tool. She didn't want to learn a new harness, so she had her Claude Code agent run the Muse Wonder benchmark tasks headlessly. The tasks included inbox triage, email batching and long-term research, and she compared the results with other models.
How it went
Muse Wonder was her favorite model on all four agentic tasks, with a good coworker-like voice and strong long-running work. It also did well on backend coding and basic writing. It was weak on design, prototypes and frontend.
Worth knowing
Setup was the most annoying part: it needs Muse service API access plus the Muse Code install. The source gives no cost figures for any of it.
Try it yourself
with
Meta Muse
Copy prompt
Go through my inbox from the last [number] days and sort messages into: needs a reply today, can wait, and ignore. Draft short replies for the ones that need a response, and group routine messages like [newsletters, receipts] into one summary. Show me the drafts and any proposed archiving or deleting before you send or remove anything. A finished job is a prioritized list plus drafts ready for my approval.
Original source: https://www.chatprd.ai/how-i-ai/meta-muse-wonder-review
